subsystems.name: Perception encoder
subsystems.role: turns camera images and joint readings into a sequence of tokens the model can attend to.

subsystems.name: Transformer backbone
subsystems.role: models long-range dependencies between past observations, instructions and actions.

subsystems.name: Action head
subsystems.role: decodes the model's output into continuous motor commands for the robot.

subsystems.name: Training pipeline
subsystems.role: learns control policies from human demonstrations and simulated experience.

subsystems.name: Deployment runtime
subsystems.role: runs the model on the robot with low enough latency for control.

subsystems.name: Safety and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps the learned controller within safe bounds.

buildSteps.title: Collect human demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: Operators teleoperate a robot through many variations of each task, recording video, joint positions and commanded actions.

buildSteps.title: Build a simulation environment
buildSteps.detail: Physics engines model the robot and objects; randomize lighting, textures and physics to broaden experience.

buildSteps.title: Design the model
buildSteps.detail: Choose a transformer that ingests image and state tokens and outputs action tokens; set context length and action chunking.

buildSteps.title: Train in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Use imitation learning from scripted or human demonstrations, then reinforcement learning to refine policies.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune on real data
buildSteps.detail: Adapt the simulated policy to the real robot using the collected demonstration dataset, correcting for the sim-to-real gap.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Test on held-out tasks; measure success rate and failure modes; collect more data where the model fails.

buildSteps.title: Deploy on the robot
buildSteps.detail: Optimize the model for real-time inference, integrate with the robot's control bus, and run at the required control frequency.

buildSteps.title: Add safety layers
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the learned policy with action limits, a fallback controller and an emergency stop so unsafe outputs are rejected.

prerequisites.why: learning general policies needs many hours of diverse real-world manipulation data, which is expensive to collect.
simulators can generate unlimited data but still struggle to match real contact dynamics and sensor noise.

prerequisites.tech: Transformer architectures for sequential decision making
prerequisites.why: attention-based models are well established in language and vision and adapt naturally to action sequences.
onboard GPUs can run large models fast enough for robot control loops.
no standard way to prove a neural network controller is safe across all situations it may encounter.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes perform single tasks such as picking and placing with high success in controlled settings.
pathway.unlocks: proof that end-to-end control can work on real hardware.

pathway.milestone: models generalize across many tasks and several robot bodies, trained on aggregated datasets.
pathway.unlocks: reusable policies that reduce per-task engineering.

pathway.milestone: commercial humanoid robots use end-to-end control for specific jobs in warehouses or factories.
general-purpose robots learn new tasks from a few demonstrations and operate safely alongside people.
